title: NAV ADR 1+2+3 FAULT · BUSS

alert.trigger: The three ADRs are failed. Also triggers when the crew turns off all ADRs below FL 250 because speed stays unreliable.

effectivity.note: ECAM procedure and STATUS: one version for all HS-TX. QRH ALL ADR OFF differs: HS-TXA..TXO also lose both FMS.

summary: Below FL 250, if the speed stays unreliable, the crew turns off all three ADRs. Both PFDs then show the Backup Speed Scale (BUSS) based on angle of attack and the backup altitude scale, GPS altitude. Fly the green band with pitch and thrust. The BUSS cannot be switched back. Do not use speed brakes, and control the cabin pressure manually.

tables.caption: Top to bottom on the PFD.
rows: Excessive speed, decreasing the margin to the maximum structural speed
Excessive speed, keeping an appropriate margin to the maximum structural speed
Optimum target speed; in approach, the approach target speed
Too low, keeping an appropriate margin to the stall speed
Too low, reducing the margin to the stall speed

background.text: When activated, the BUSS replaces the normal speed and GPS altitude replaces the barometric altitude scale, on both PFDs, once the crew turns off all ADRs.
The BUSS comes from the angle of attack and depends on the slat/flap configuration.
Backup altitude scale: current GPS altitude with two amber dashes over the last two digits, a GPS ALT flag, and no vertical speed indication.
Speed brakes change the speed-to-AOA relationship, so the BUSS may then give erroneous data.

technique.text: Before retracting the next flap setting fly the upper part of the green band; before extending it, the lower part. This limits excursions into the amber zones.
Any longitudinal stick input changes the AOA, so the BUSS must move. If it does not, disregard it.
While the BUSS is active: cabin pressure controlled manually, HUD not used if installed, FPV available on one or both PFDs depending on the ADIRS standard.

gaps.text: "BAS" is not an abbreviation in the supplied manuals: the FCOM says Backup Altitude Scale and the PDP says Back-Up Altitude Scale.
PDP mentions a "reversible BUSS (if installed)". The FCOM states activation is not reversible for all HS-TX; the reversible modification is listed for HS-TO only. This brief follows the FCOM.
The flow order and PF/PM split of the QRH part are arranged from the QRH lines and AOP-30-30; no PDP slide gives the turns.
